1	# Playthrough Strategy
2	
3	Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
4	its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
5	area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.
6	
7	## General Strategy
8	
9	- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
10	
11	## Recruiting Units
12	
13	In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.
14	
15	The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.
16	
17	## Promoting Units
18	
19	Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.
20	
21	In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.
22	
23	## Broad strategy notes
24	
25	Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.
26	
27	- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
28	- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
29	- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
30	- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
31	- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
32	- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
33	- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
34	- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
35	- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.
36	- Open the Attack list for your main fighters every few turns: weapons run out silently, and a unit with no weapon has no Attack, so a blind `A` chooses the next entry (Take, Item). Empty ballistae look manned; if no Attack appears at 2 tiles, nobody is on them.

521	**Agent notes:**
522	
523	- Won on turn 50 by s01 on attempt 1, picking up a game already on turn 24 (Hector was 15/40). No deaths. Farina not recruited: only about 9,000G available, never spoke to her.
524	- Any unit can score, not just the lord: Canas (NE), Dart (N), Dart (SW). Points persist after the unit leaves. Seize never appears. Clearing all enemies does not win, and Door Keys, ruins and shops do nothing for points.
525	- Hector stood on the SW gate on t24 and I backed out without Waiting. Waiting there would have scored at once and saved a long detour. On a retry: Wait on the nearest gate first.
526	- Enemies seen: cavaliers, steel-bow archers, and a Bishop with Purge (range 3-10). Monks arrived in pairs near the NE castle from about t38; none appeared after Canas held that gate from t43, though I can't prove the cause.
527	- Lake is impassable even for Dart, and the eastern mountains block walkers. The route to the north runs over the middle bridge, along the shore, then over the wide bridge. Ballistae hit across the lake (5 uses each, Wil used one up); several unused ones remain.
528	- Vendor (Mend, Thunder, Lightning, Flux) and Armory (steel weapons) are just north of the eastern mountains. Bought one Steel axe for Hawkeye (360G), but did not check his inventory afterwards. Funds at handover about 8,697G.
529	- Army at handover: Hector Lv18 (42 HP, brave/hand/steel axes, hammer), Hawkeye Lv6 (Killer axe, low on uses), Wil gained a level (31 max HP) and has only the bow I saw him fire; I never opened his inventory. Canas (Nosferatu, Heal, 2 Door Keys) had a level-up screen, level unconfirmed. Dart Lv8 (steel axe, hand axe, torch). Only these five plus Merlinus are on the Unit list, which is a very thin army.
530	- Canas is fragile against Purge and took several hits unnoticed: read every HP after each enemy phase. Nosferatu on Monks heals him safely.
531	- Ending: saved to the highlighted Ch. 25 slot (the save prompt's default), which is the one assumed to be in use. Chapter 26 title card was missed; Preparations shows "Chapter 26", objective Survive.

546	
547	- Objective as shown: Survive, 11 turns (HUD "1/11 Turn").
548	- s02 attempt 1 lost on the first enemy phase: Lyn died beside Hector on open plain and the game went straight to GAME OVER. Lyn's death ends the chapter. I had not read her HP before placing her.
549	- Start: north group Hector, Lyn, Eliwood, Louise, Pent; south group Wil, Dart, Canas, Hawkeye, Matthew, Ninian, Merlinus's tent. Louise and Pent are controllable but L skips them; select them with the cursor.
550	- Enemies seen: mage and shaman just west of the north group, brigands on the peaks between the groups, steel-lance wyverns far NE, and riders, archers and more brigands south. They reach the north group on enemy phase 1.
551	- Two ballistae sit by the south group. Wil rides one (Ride, then Attack): 14 damage. Ninian's Dance gave a second shot and killed a 24 HP archer on t1.

553	s02 attempt 2 (won, turn 11):
554	
555	- Died: Dart (t3 enemy phase, left on the flank and hit by two wyverns) and Wil (t11 enemy phase, left on the ballista beside two wyverns after his last shot). Pulling both back would probably have saved them. Vaida was never attacked on my phase and spoke in Ch. 27's opening, so she is alive for Ch. 29.
556	- Lords stayed east on t1, which solved the opening. Lyn was at 7/23 from t4 after I attacked with her for 2 damage a hit, so Hector carried her from t5 to the end. Eliwood sat boxed in beside Hector, dropped to 8/21 on two separate enemy phases, and Pent healed him both times.
557	- What worked: Louise's silver bow one-shots wyverns from 2 tiles; Pent's long-range staff heals across the mountains; Hawkeye kills nearly everything he reaches. Wyverns come in waves from the castle (north) and the south/east from about t3.
558	- Ninian and Nils left the map in a scripted event on t4 enemy phase; I did not see Ninian afterwards and did not check whether she is still on the Unit list.
559	- Level-ups seen: Wil Sniper Lv6 (now dead), Hawkeye Berserker Lv8 (Str 21, Spd 12, Def 14). Hawkeye's Killer axe is down from 12 uses; Steel axe was bought last chapter.
560	- Army at handover: Hector Lv18, Hawkeye Lv8, Pent Sage Lv6, Louise Sniper Lv4, Canas Druid Lv8, Lyn Lv13, Eliwood Lv4, Matthew Lv4 (no weapon). No healer besides Pent and Canas. I did not re-read the Unit list after the win.
561	- Merlinus was last seen alive at 18 HP or less with wyverns adjacent on t11; his survival is unconfirmed.
562	- Next time: on the last turns pull ranged units off ballistae when they run out or get surrounded, and never leave a low-HP unit on an open flank. Before attacking with Lyn or Eliwood, read their damage: both do very little to wyverns.
563	- Ending: saved over the highlighted Ch. 26 slot (the one in use); no other choice appeared.

584	- Lost: Matthew, in the t1 enemy phase. I saw "Leila..." on screen, then he was off the map and off the Unit list; I did not see the blow, so the death is inferred. A Bolting mage and a Purge bishop (both range 3-10) also took Eliwood to 5/21. Next time, carry both lords and hide or carry Matthew before ending t1.
585	- Recruited: Harken (Hector Talk, t19), Lv8+ Hero with Brave sword, 41 max HP, and he carried the end of the chapter. Karel never appeared. Harken walks round outside the walls and drove Merlinus off the map on t17; Merlinus left by script, unharmed as far as I saw.

Only (11,3)-style one tile touches the throne from the south.
587	- Long-range tomes run out. Bait them with carried lords and kill the casters over walls: Louise's silver bow reaches 2 tiles through any wall. Waves of about 10 steel-lance wyverns come down the river from t5 and die to Louise, Pent and counters.
588	- Three chests NW of the throne: Pent stood on two with a Chest key and got no Chest command. I don't know why, and I did not try the third. Pent still holds that key.
589	- Items lost: Canas's Nosferatu broke (t7), Pent's Physic broke (t30), Hawkeye's Killer axe was on its last use on t13. Healing is now only Canas's Heal (about 8 uses). Hector's Heaven Seal is greyed out at Lv18-19, so he cannot promote yet.
590	- Levels seen last: Hector 19, Pent Sage 9+, Louise Sniper 7+, Canas Druid 9, Hawkeye Berserker 9, Harken gained at least one level. Lyn stayed 13 and Eliwood 4, carried all chapter. Louise was about half HP after Kenneth's counter, then healed.

592	- Next time: 31 turns was slow but safe. The waiting at the gate for Harken (t16-19) was worth it.

594	### Chapter 28 — Battle before Dawn
595

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.
- Open the Attack list for your main fighters every few turns: weapons run out silently, and a unit with no weapon has no Attack, so a blind `A` chooses the next entry (Take, Item). Empty ballistae look manned; if no Attack appears at 2 tiles, nobody is on them.

**Agent notes:**

- Won on turn 50 by s01 on attempt 1, picking up a game already on turn 24 (Hector was 15/40). No deaths. Farina not recruited: only about 9,000G available, never spoke to her.
- Any unit can score, not just the lord: Canas (NE), Dart (N), Dart (SW). Points persist after the unit leaves. Seize never appears. Clearing all enemies does not win, and Door Keys, ruins and shops do nothing for points.
- Hector stood on the SW gate on t24 and I backed out without Waiting. Waiting there would have scored at once and saved a long detour. On a retry: Wait on the nearest gate first.
- Enemies seen: cavaliers, steel-bow archers, and a Bishop with Purge (range 3-10). Monks arrived in pairs near the NE castle from about t38; none appeared after Canas held that gate from t43, though I can't prove the cause.
- Lake is impassable even for Dart, and the eastern mountains block walkers. The route to the north runs over the middle bridge, along the shore, then over the wide bridge. Ballistae hit across the lake (5 uses each, Wil used one up); several unused ones remain.
- Vendor (Mend, Thunder, Lightning, Flux) and Armory (steel weapons) are just north of the eastern mountains. Bought one Steel axe for Hawkeye (360G), but did not check his inventory afterwards. Funds at handover about 8,697G.
- Army at handover: Hector Lv18 (42 HP, brave/hand/steel axes, hammer), Hawkeye Lv6 (Killer axe, low on uses), Wil gained a level (31 max HP) and has only the bow I saw him fire; I never opened his inventory. Canas (Nosferatu, Heal, 2 Door Keys) had a level-up screen, level unconfirmed. Dart Lv8 (steel axe, hand axe, torch). Only these five plus Merlinus are on the Unit list, which is a very thin army.
- Canas is fragile against Purge and took several hits unnoticed: read every HP after each enemy phase. Nosferatu on Monks heals him safely.
- Ending: saved to the highlighted Ch. 25 slot (the save prompt's default), which is the one assumed to be in use. Chapter 26 title card was missed; Preparations shows "Chapter 26", objective Survive.

### Chapter 26 — Unfulfilled Heart

**Objectives:**

**Recruits:**

None.

Vaida appears here as an enemy. Do **not** kill her; she must survive this chapter to be recruitable in Chapter 29.

**Agent notes:**

- Objective as shown: Survive, 11 turns (HUD "1/11 Turn").
- s02 attempt 1 lost on the first enemy phase: Lyn died beside Hector on open plain and the game went straight to GAME OVER. Lyn's death ends the chapter. I had not read her HP before placing her.
- Start: north group Hector, Lyn, Eliwood, Louise, Pent; south group Wil, Dart, Canas, Hawkeye, Matthew, Ninian, Merlinus's tent. Louise and Pent are controllable but L skips them; select them with the cursor.
- Enemies seen: mage and shaman just west of the north group, brigands on the peaks between the groups, steel-lance wyverns far NE, and riders, archers and more brigands south. They reach the north group on enemy phase 1.
- Two ballistae sit by the south group. Wil rides one (Ride, then Attack): 14 damage. Ninian's Dance gave a second shot and killed a 24 HP archer on t1.

s02 attempt 2 (won, turn 11):

- Died: Dart (t3 enemy phase, left on the flank and hit by two wyverns) and Wil (t11 enemy phase, left on the ballista beside two wyverns after his last shot). Pulling both back would probably have saved them. Vaida was never attacked on my phase and spoke in Ch. 27's opening, so she is alive for Ch. 29.
- Lords stayed east on t1, which solved the opening. Lyn was at 7/23 from t4 after I attacked with her for 2 damage a hit, so Hector carried her from t5 to the end. Eliwood sat boxed in beside Hector, dropped to 8/21 on two separate enemy phases, and Pent healed him both times.
- What worked: Louise's silver bow one-shots wyverns from 2 tiles; Pent's long-range staff heals across the mountains; Hawkeye kills nearly everything he reaches. Wyverns come in waves from the castle (north) and the south/east from about t3.
- Ninian and Nils left the map in a scripted event on t4 enemy phase; I did not see Ninian afterwards and did not check whether she is still on the Unit list.
- Level-ups seen: Wil Sniper Lv6 (now dead), Hawkeye Berserker Lv8 (Str 21, Spd 12, Def 14). Hawkeye's Killer axe is down from 12 uses; Steel axe was bought last chapter.
- Army at handover: Hector Lv18, Hawkeye Lv8, Pent Sage Lv6, Louise Sniper Lv4, Canas Druid Lv8, Lyn Lv13, Eliwood Lv4, Matthew Lv4 (no weapon). No healer besides Pent and Canas. I did not re-read the Unit list after the win.
- Merlinus was last seen alive at 18 HP or less with wyverns adjacent on t11; his survival is unconfirmed.
- Next time: on the last turns pull ranged units off ballistae when they run out or get surrounded, and never leave a low-HP unit on an open flank. Before attacking with Lyn or Eliwood, read their damage: both do very little to wyverns.
- Ending: saved over the highlighted Ch. 26 slot (the one in use); no other choice appeared.

### Chapter 27 — Pale Flower of Darkness

**Objectives:**

Seize throne (Preparations text). Throne is in the far NE; the boss Kenneth (Bishop, Lv13, 41 HP, Atk 31, Aura range 1-2) sits on it.

**Recruits:**

**Agent notes:**

s03 attempt 1 (won, Hector seized on turn 31):

- Lost: Matthew, in the t1 enemy phase. I saw "Leila..." on screen, then he was off the map and off the Unit list; I did not see the blow, so the death is inferred. A Bolting mage and a Purge bishop (both range 3-10) also took Eliwood to 5/21. Next time, carry both lords and hide or carry Matthew before ending t1.
- Recruited: Harken (Hector Talk, t19), Lv8+ Hero with Brave sword, 41 max HP, and he carried the end of the chapter. Karel never appeared. Harken walks round outside the walls and drove Merlinus off the map on t17; Merlinus left by script, unharmed as far as I saw.
- Route: south gate is a Door (key needed), then the courtyard, the gap in its north wall, the long hall, west to the gap by the bishop's room, the room north of it, east through the pillar gap, the big archer court, then the gap in its north wall to the throne. Only (11,3)-style one tile touches the throne from the south.
- Long-range tomes run out. Bait them with carried lords and kill the casters over walls: Louise's silver bow reaches 2 tiles through any wall. Waves of about 10 steel-lance wyverns come down the river from t5 and die to Louise, Pent and counters.
- Three chests NW of the throne: Pent stood on two with a Chest key and got no Chest command. I don't know why, and I did not try the third. Pent still holds that key.
- Items lost: Canas's Nosferatu broke (t7), Pent's Physic broke (t30), Hawkeye's Killer axe was on its last use on t13. Healing is now only Canas's Heal (about 8 uses). Hector's Heaven Seal is greyed out at Lv18-19, so he cannot promote yet.
- Levels seen last: Hector 19, Pent Sage 9+, Louise Sniper 7+, Canas Druid 9, Hawkeye Berserker 9, Harken gained at least one level. Lyn stayed 13 and Eliwood 4, carried all chapter. Louise was about half HP after Kenneth's counter, then healed.
- Save prompt: chose the highlighted Ch. 27 slot, then Save. Deploying Merlinus was Yes; he had no effect on the fight.
- Next time: 31 turns was slow but safe. The waiting at the gate for Harken (t16-19) was worth it.

### Chapter 28 — Battle before Dawn

**Objectives:**

Guard Zephiel (Preparations text); "Protect Zephiel for 15 turns" (Status screen); HUD counts "1/15 Turn". Fog map.

**Recruits:**

| character  | starts as | recruit with / action     | important condition                                              |

**Agent notes:**

s04 attempt 1 (lost, GAME OVER on t6 enemy phase): Zephiel was killed while my army was still in the north. Three enemies stood next to him at the start of t6.

- Layout: party starts in the walled north yard. East stairs lead to a corridor, whose south wall has a locked door (Door key on Canas; Hawkeye also received one at the end of t1). South of it is the north hall. From there, stairs on the east side lead round to Nino's corridor (Hector reached her tile range by t7) and the far south hall. Zephiel's room opens only on its south side, from the south hall. Walking there takes about 10 turns; enemies arrive by t5.
- Pent one-shots casters: Elfire about 26 x2 at 100%, Bolting (range 3-10) 21 x2 at 100%, even through walls. Keep Bolting and use it from the north hall on whoever reaches Zephiel. On t3 I sent Bolting to the convoy by pressing A on a full-inventory list; do not repeat.
- Louise has no bow. An enemy thief empties the chests from about t5 (Brave lance taken t5).

s04 attempt 2 (lost, GAME OVER on t5 enemy phase; Zephiel said "Mother..." and fell): I pressed Start through the intro and skipped Preparations by accident, so no Torch and no Merlinus. Press Start once at a time and stop at the Preparations screen.

- Pent waited with Bolting on the yard's south edge (Zephiel's column, 11 rows below Hector's start), but had no target on t3 or t5: fog hides the attackers from there.
- The swordsman on the east stairs drops a Door key and a Lockpick. Harken opened the door on t3 after Hawkeye passed him a key. Bishop and Thunder mage then stand in the door on t4; Harken and Hector kill them.
- Next: Preparations first. Swap Pent forward with Formation, give him Bolting and a Torch carrier beside him, and get him into the hall by t5, near the brick strip above Zephiel's room.

s04 attempt 3 (lost, GAME OVER on t6 enemy phase): Ursula appears in the south hall on the t6 enemy phase and hit Hector from far away, about 26 x2 with 43 max HP; he died. **Correction to my attempt 1 note above: that game over followed the same Ursula event and Hector's "No! Not here! Not now...", so it was very probably Hector's death, not Zephiel's.** Zephiel's death reads "Mother..." (attempt 2).

- This opening held Zephiel at 20/20 through t6: Preparations gave Pent Bolting and Harken the Torch and Door key; Formation put Pent on Louise's tile and Harken on the far-east blue tile (Hector cannot be moved). Harken opened the door on t2. Pent stood at the hall's south edge above Zephiel's room by t5 and shot a Swordslayer in the south hall through the walls.
- Next: have Hawkeye Rescue Hector (his menu offers it when adjacent) before ending t6, so Ursula cannot target him. Then kill her.

s07 (picked up attempt 4 on t6; lost, GAME OVER on t10 enemy phase; Zephiel said "Mother..."):

- Carrying Hector with Hawkeye worked: Ursula never targeted him through t9. She and about 10 enemies spent t6-t9 in the south hall attacking Jaffar.
- Nino is recruitable: Hawkeye dropped Hector in her dead-end corridor on t9 and Hector talked on t10. Hector was at Lv20 on t6.
- Zephiel's killer came from fog along the west carpet and struck in one enemy phase, so a long-range shot alone cannot save him. One intruder was already 2 tiles away on t8 (Pent's Bolting killed it). Someone must be in his room by about t8, with his two open neighbour tiles (carpet side and floor side) blocked.
- Harken was not on the Unit list in attempt 4. Check that he is deployed.

s07 attempt 5 (lost, GAME OVER on t10 enemy phase; a sword enemy inside the room killed Zephiel, 20 HP, from just below his tile):

- Rush worked but was a turn or two late: Harken opened the door on t3, the hall was clear on t5, and Hawkeye and Harken reached the south hall on t8. On t9 enemies were already on Zephiel's stairs. We killed about 12 enemies with no losses. Hector and the lords in the yard were never touched.
- Plan for next attempt: the room's only entrance is the stairs from the south hall, about 2 tiles wide. Two units at the top of the stairs seal it, and Zephiel is too far from there for ranged attacks. Reach it by t8 at the latest.
- Save time: on t1 Harken should use all 6 Move past the east stairs into the corridor so he can open the door on t2. Hawkeye must use full Move every turn. A fog ambush (red heavy plus bishop) waits just south of the door, so expect to be stopped there.
- Preparations: use Trade, then Trd or Trnsfr, and check the hand before pressing A (Give all sits right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy). Formation only moved Harken; Pent refused. Start on the Formation screen shows a minimap, and Select then Start begins the fight.
- Pent's Bolting: 5 uses, doubling spends 2. Save them for enemies inside Zephiel's room. Move Pent west along the hall's south edge to reach the stairs.

s07 attempt 6 (lost, GAME OVER on t5 enemy phase, three enemies around Zephiel): I opened the door on t2 and sped south, and the door ambush never happened. My read is that those enemies then went straight to Zephiel instead of stopping to fight, though I can't prove the cause. Rushing past them is worse than fighting them. Good opening to keep: t1 Harken full Move into the corridor, Hawkeye's Hand axe kills the Swordreaver fighter from 2 tiles (drops a Door key). Do not open the door before t3.

s07 attempt 7 key discovery: Zephiel can be RESCUED. A unit standing on the carpet tile in front of his alcove gets Rescue (Hawkeye Aid 15, Zephiel Con 7), and a carried Zephiel cannot be targeted. Hawkeye did this on t11. Zephiel walks to the back-wall alcove by about t9, and that alcove has only the one open neighbour.

s07 attempt 7 (WON, survived through t15; "Protect Zephiel for 15 turns" per the Status screen):

- What won it: fight at the door as above, Pent's Bolting on whoever reached Zephiel (t6, t8), then Hawkeye rescued Zephiel on t11 and stood in the alcove from t12 to t15. # Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.
- Open the Attack list for your main fighters every few turns: weapons run out silently, and a unit with no weapon has no Attack, so a blind `A` chooses the next entry (Take, Item). Empty ballistae look manned; if no Attack appears at 2 tiles, nobody is on them.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.
- Open the Attack list for your main fighters every few turns: weapons run out silently, and a unit with no weapon has no Attack, so a blind `A` chooses the next entry (Take, Item). Empty ballistae look manned; if no Attack appears at 2 tiles, nobody is on them.

- What worked: Louise's silver bow one-shots wyverns from 2 tiles; Pent's long-range staff heals across the mountains; Hawkeye kills nearly everything he reaches. Wyverns come in waves from the castle (north) and the south/east from about t3.
- Ninian and Nils left the map in a scripted event on t4 enemy phase; I did not see Ninian afterwards and did not check whether she is still on the Unit list.
- Level-ups seen: Wil Sniper Lv6 (now dead), Hawkeye Berserker Lv8 (Str 21, Spd 12, Def 14). Hawkeye's Killer axe is down from 12 uses; Steel axe was bought last chapter.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.
- Open the Attack list for your main fighters every few turns: weapons run out silently, and a unit with no weapon has no Attack, so a blind `A` chooses the next entry (Take, Item). Empty ballistae look manned; if no Attack appears at 2 tiles, nobody is on them.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.
- In shops, press and screenshot per purchase: a cursor press during the "Anything else?" text gets dropped, and the next A buys the wrong item. Backing out of an unused shop undoes the unit's move, so it can scout others.
- Open the Attack list for your main fighters every few turns: weapons run out silently, and a unit with no weapon has no Attack, so a blind `A` chooses the next entry (Take, Item). Empty ballistae look manned; if no Attack appears at 2 tiles, nobody is on them.

### Chapter 25 — Crazed Beast

**Agent notes:**

- Won on turn 50 by s01 on attempt 1, picking up a game already on turn 24 (Hector was 15/40). No deaths. Farina not recruited: only about 9,000G available, never spoke to her.
- Any unit can score, not just the lord: Canas (NE), Dart (N), Dart (SW). Points persist after the unit leaves. Seize never appears. Clearing all enemies does not win, and Door Keys, ruins and shops do nothing for points.
- Hector stood on the SW gate on t24 and I backed out without Waiting. Waiting there would have scored at once and saved a long detour. On a retry: Wait on the nearest gate first.
- Enemies seen: cavaliers, steel-bow archers, and a Bishop with Purge (range 3-10). Monks arrived in pairs near the NE castle from about t38; none appeared after Canas held that gate from t43, though I can't prove the cause.
- Lake is impassable even for Dart, and the eastern mountains block walkers. The route to the north runs over the middle bridge, along the shore, then over the wide bridge. Ballistae hit across the lake (5 uses each, Wil used one up); several unused ones remain.
- Vendor (Mend, Thunder, Lightning, Flux) and Armory (steel weapons) are just north of the eastern mountains. Bought one Steel axe for Hawkeye (360G), but did not check his inventory afterwards. Funds at handover about 8,697G.
- Army at handover: Hector Lv18 (42 HP, brave/hand/steel axes, hammer), Hawkeye Lv6 (Killer axe, low on uses), Wil gained a level (31 max HP) and has only the bow I saw him fire; I never opened his inventory. Canas (Nosferatu, Heal, 2 Door Keys) had a level-up screen, level unconfirmed. Dart Lv8 (steel axe, hand axe, torch). Only these five plus Merlinus are on the Unit list, which is a very thin army.
- Canas is fragile against Purge and took several hits unnoticed: read every HP after each enemy phase. Nosferatu on Monks heals him safely.
- Ending: saved to the highlighted Ch. 25 slot (the save prompt's default), which is the one assumed to be in use. Chapter 26 title card was missed; Preparations shows "Chapter 26", objective Survive.

### Chapter 26 — Unfulfilled Heart

**Objectives:**

Survive for 11 turns (Preparations: "Survive"; HUD counts "1/11 Turn" up to "Last Turn"). The win triggers after the enemy phase of turn 11.

**Recruits:**

None.

Vaida appears here as an enemy. Do **not** kill her; she must survive this chapter to be recruitable in Chapter 29.

**Agent notes:**

- Objective as shown: Survive, 11 turns (HUD "1/11 Turn").
- s02 attempt 1 lost on the first enemy phase: Lyn died beside Hector on open plain and the game went straight to GAME OVER. Lyn's death ends the chapter. I had not read her HP before placing her.
- Start: north group Hector, Lyn, Eliwood, Louise, Pent; south group Wil, Dart, Canas, Hawkeye, Matthew, Ninian, Merlinus's tent. Louise and Pent are controllable but L skips them; select them with the cursor.
- Enemies seen: mage and shaman just west of the north group, brigands on the peaks between the groups, steel-lance wyverns far NE, and riders, archers and more brigands south. They reach the north group on enemy phase 1.
- Two ballistae sit by the south group. Wil rides one (Ride, then Attack): 14 damage. Ninian's Dance gave a second shot and killed a 24 HP archer on t1.

s02 attempt 2 (won, turn 11):

- Died: Dart (t3 enemy phase, left on the flank and hit by two wyverns) and Wil (t11 enemy phase, left on the ballista beside two wyverns after his last shot). Pulling both back would probably have saved them. Vaida was never attacked on my phase and spoke in Ch. 27's opening, so she is alive for Ch. 29.
- Lords stayed east on t1, which solved the opening. Lyn was at 7/23 from t4 after I attacked with her for 2 damage a hit, so Hector carried her from t5 to the end. Eliwood sat boxed in beside Hector, dropped to 8/21 on two separate enemy phases, and Pent healed him both times.
- What worked: Louise's silver bow one-shots wyverns from 2 tiles; Pent's long-range staff heals across the mountains; Hawkeye kills nearly everything he reaches. Wyverns come in waves from the castle (north) and the south/east from about t3.
- Ninian and Nils left the map in a scripted event on t4 enemy phase; I did not see Ninian afterwards and did not check whether she is still on the Unit list.
- Level-ups seen: Wil Sniper Lv6 (now dead), Hawkeye Berserker Lv8 (Str 21, Spd 12, Def 14). Hawkeye's Killer axe is down from 12 uses; Steel axe was bought last chapter.
- Army at handover: Hector Lv18, Hawkeye Lv8, Pent Sage Lv6, Louise Sniper Lv4, Canas Druid Lv8, Lyn Lv13, Eliwood Lv4, Matthew Lv4 (no weapon). No healer besides Pent and Canas. I did not re-read the Unit list after the win.
- Merlinus was last seen alive at 18 HP or less with wyverns adjacent on t11; his survival is unconfirmed.
- Next time: on the last turns pull ranged units off ballistae when they run out or get surrounded, and never leave a low-HP unit on an open flank. Before attacking with Lyn or Eliwood, read their damage: both do very little to wyverns.
- Ending: saved over the highlighted Ch. 26 slot (the one in use); no other choice appeared.

### Chapter 27 — Pale Flower of Darkness

**Objectives:**

Seize throne (Preparations text). Throne is in the far NE; the boss Kenneth (Bishop, Lv13, 41 HP, Atk 31, Aura range 1-2) sits on it.

**Recruits:**

| character  | starts as | recruit with / action                                 | important condition                                           |
| ---------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **karel**  | green npc | **hector or lyn**                                     | mutually exclusive with harken; see the note below this table |
| **harken** | enemy     | **eliwood, marcus, lowen, hector, oswin, or isadora** | mutually exclusive with karel; see the note below this table  |

Depending on various circumstances, you will only see one of the two on the map. You cannot get both.

**Agent notes:**

s03 attempt 1 (won, Hector seized on turn 31):

- Lost: Matthew, in the t1 enemy phase. I saw "Leila..." on screen, then he was off the map and off the Unit list; I did not see the blow, so the death is inferred. A Bolting mage and a Purge bishop (both range 3-10) also took Eliwood to 5/21. Next time, carry both lords and hide or carry Matthew before ending t1.
- Recruited: Harken (Hector Talk, t19), Lv8+ Hero with Brave sword, 41 max HP, and he carried the end of the chapter. Karel never appeared. Harken walks round outside the walls and drove Merlinus off the map on t17; Merlinus left by script, unharmed as far as I saw.
- Route: south gate is a Door (key needed), then the courtyard, the gap in its north wall, the long hall, west to the gap by the bishop's room, the room north of it, east through the pillar gap, the big archer court, then the gap in its north wall to the throne. Only (11,3)-style one tile touches the throne from the south.
- Long-range tomes run out. Bait them with carried lords and kill the casters over walls: Louise's silver bow reaches 2 tiles through any wall. Waves of about 10 steel-lance wyverns come down the river from t5 and die to Louise, Pent and counters.
- Three chests NW of the throne: Pent stood on two with a Chest key and got no Chest command. I don't know why, and I did not try the third. Pent still holds that key.
- Items lost: Canas's Nosferatu broke (t7), Pent's Physic broke (t30), Hawkeye's Killer axe was on its last use on t13. Healing is now only Canas's Heal (about 8 uses). Hector's Heaven Seal is greyed out at Lv18-19, so he cannot promote yet.
- Levels seen last: Hector 19, Pent Sage 9+, Louise Sniper 7+, Canas Druid 9, Hawkeye Berserker 9, Harken gained at least one level. Lyn stayed 13 and Eliwood 4, carried all chapter. Louise was about half HP after Kenneth's counter, then healed.
- Save prompt: chose the highlighted Ch. 27 slot, then Save. Deploying Merlinus was Yes; he had no effect on the fight.
- Next time: 31 turns was slow but safe. The waiting at the gate for Harken (t16-19) was worth it.

### Chapter 28 — Battle before Dawn

**Objectives:**

Guard Zephiel (Preparations text); "Protect Zephiel for 15 turns" (Status screen); HUD counts "1/15 Turn". Fog map.

**Recruits:**

| character  | starts as | recruit with / action     | important condition                                              |
| ---------- | --------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **nino**   | green npc | **hector or lyn**         | keep her alive afterward                                         |
| **jaffar** | green npc | **nino must talk to him** | both must survive ch. 28; jaffar then joins automatically in 28x |

**Agent notes:**

s04 attempt 1 (lost, GAME OVER on t6 enemy phase): Zephiel was killed while my army was still in the north. Three enemies stood next to him at the start of t6.

- Layout: party starts in the walled north yard. East stairs lead to a corridor, whose south wall has a locked door (Door key on Canas; Hawkeye also received one at the end of t1). South of it is the north hall. From there, stairs on the east side lead round to Nino's corridor (Hector reached her tile range by t7) and the far south hall. Zephiel's room opens only on its south side, from the south hall. Walking there takes about 10 turns; enemies arrive by t5.
- Pent one-shots casters: Elfire about 26 x2 at 100%, Bolting (range 3-10) 21 x2 at 100%, even through walls. Keep Bolting and use it from the north hall on whoever reaches Zephiel. On t3 I sent Bolting to the convoy by pressing A on a full-inventory list; do not repeat.
- Louise has no bow. An enemy thief empties the chests from about t5 (Brave lance taken t5).

s04 attempt 2 (lost, GAME OVER on t5 enemy phase; Zephiel said "Mother..." and fell): I pressed Start through the intro and skipped Preparations by accident, so no Torch and no Merlinus. Press Start once at a time and stop at the Preparations screen.

- Pent waited with Bolting on the yard's south edge (Zephiel's column, 11 rows below Hector's start), but had no target on t3 or t5: fog hides the attackers from there.
- The swordsman on the east stairs drops a Door key and a Lockpick. Harken opened the door on t3 after Hawkeye passed him a key. Bishop and Thunder mage then stand in the door on t4; Harken and Hector kill them.
- Next: Preparations first. Swap Pent forward with Formation, give him Bolting and a Torch carrier beside him, and get him into the hall by t5, near the brick strip above Zephiel's room.

s04 attempt 3 (lost, GAME OVER on t6 enemy phase): Ursula appears in the south hall on the t6 enemy phase and hit Hector from far away, about 26 x2 with 43 max HP; he died. **Correction to my attempt 1 note above: that game over followed the same Ursula event and Hector's "No! Not here! Not now...", so it was very probably Hector's death, not Zephiel's.** Zephiel's death reads "Mother..." (attempt 2).

- This opening held Zephiel at 20/20 through t6: Preparations gave Pent Bolting and Harken the Torch and Door key; Formation put Pent on Louise's tile and Harken on the far-east blue tile (Hector cannot be moved). Harken opened the door on t2. Pent stood at the hall's south edge above Zephiel's room by t5 and shot a Swordslayer in the south hall through the walls.
- Next: have Hawkeye Rescue Hector (his menu offers it when adjacent) before ending t6, so Ursula cannot target him. Then kill her.

s07 (picked up attempt 4 on t6; lost, GAME OVER on t10 enemy phase; Zephiel said "Mother..."):

- Carrying Hector with Hawkeye worked: Ursula never targeted him through t9. She and about 10 enemies spent t6-t9 in the south hall attacking Jaffar.
- Nino is recruitable: Hawkeye dropped Hector in her dead-end corridor on t9 and Hector talked on t10. Hector was at Lv20 on t6.
- Zephiel's killer came from fog along the west carpet and struck in one enemy phase, so a long-range shot alone cannot save him. One intruder was already 2 tiles away on t8 (Pent's Bolting killed it). Someone must be in his room by about t8, with his two open neighbour tiles (carpet side and floor side) blocked.
- Harken was not on the Unit list in attempt 4. Check that he is deployed.

s07 attempt 5 (lost, GAME OVER on t10 enemy phase; a sword enemy inside the room killed Zephiel, 20 HP, from just below his tile):
